La sonde géothermique est un tube en U (:
The geothermal probe is a U-shaped tube (high-density polyethylene) inserted into a vertical borehole 80 to 200 m deep. A heat-transfer fluid — glycol water — circulates in a closed loop, never coming into contact with the rock or the groundwater. It captures the thermal energy of the ground, stable at around 10–14 °C all year round, and transfers it to the heat pump.

The heat pump boosts this energy to produce hot water at 35–55 °C, supplying the heating (underfloor heating or low-temperature radiators) and domestic hot water. In summer the cycle reverses: the building's heat is dissipated into the ground, providing natural cooling with no significant extra consumption.

Le forage géothermique consiste à forer: Geothermal drilling consists of drilling vertical boreholes to install closed-loop geothermal probes. These probes, made from durable synthetic materials, contain a heat-transfer fluid (water or a mixture of water and monopropylene glycol) that circulates in a closed loop. This fluid extracts heat from the ground and transfers it to your heat pump system. The length and depth of the boreholes are calculated when sizing the system, in order to optimise energy efficiency.
